prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
competitors_mentioned: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for every Houston homeowner — the best choice depends on your location, the type/age of your system, how quickly you need service, and whether you want a low-cost repair or a longer warranty/maintenance relationship.

To help you pick the right company, here’s a quick plan and some options:

How to choose a good AC repair company
- Verify licensing and insurance: confirm the technician is registered with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) and has general liability insurance. Technicians who handle refrigerant should have EPA Section 608 certification.
- Check reviews and complaints: look at Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, and the BBB for recent feedback and complaint resolution.
- Ask about fees and warranties: get a written estimate. Ask about diagnostic fees, parts & labor warranties, and whether estimates are flat-rate or hourly.
- Ask about experience with your system: confirm they’ve worked on your brand/model and refrigerant type (R-22 vs R-410A).
- Availability and response time: if it’s an emergency, ask about after-hours/overnight service and typical arrival windows.
- Get 2–3 quotes for any major repair or replacement.

Well-known Houston companies to consider
- John Moore Services (large, Houston-based; offers emergency service and maintenance plans)
- Abacus Plumbing, AC & Electrical (local company with full-service offerings)
- Baker Brothers Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston-area specialists)
- Franchises operating in Houston: One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, ARS/Rescue Rooter (options if you prefer a national brand)

(I can look up top-rated providers near you and compare recent reviews if you give your ZIP code.)

If you want, tell me:
- your ZIP code
- whether this is an emergency
- your AC brand/age and the problem symptoms

I’ll find a few highly rated local companies, note their typical fees/warranties (if available), and recommend the best next step.
